body:
## Destination
A full autonomous plan that builds tigerstore, a drop-in etcd replacement for Kubernetes: same etcd API, consensus with go.etcd.io/raft, fully new custom storage designed from what one CPU core can do at most. It passes strong e2e, deterministic simulation and chaos tests, and beats etcd on max object count and max write throughput with similar or lower latency.

## Notes
- Domain: etcd v3 API as used by kube-apiserver, go.etcd.io/raft, custom storage engine, deterministic simulation testing, linearizability and chaos testing.
- Owner's main goal: a k8s-compatible etcd replacement that is faster and holds more objects, proven by e2e and chaos tests (packet loss, corruption, delay, latency, partitions).
- The owner decides, agents find facts.
- Owner instruction, round 6: the plan runs fully autonomous while the owner is away. Keep it small and under-specified. The design may change during the plan. Hard instruction: make it wicked fast, think outside the box, do crazy things, boil the ocean. Test it brutally and try to break it, not kindly.
- Every question is a sub-issue labelled wayfinder:<type> with question, context, options and recommendation. A decision ticket closes with an "Owner answer, round N" comment, a research ticket with its answer as a comment.
- Host facts: aarch64, 8 cores, 11 GB RAM, Go 1.27.2, 45 GB free on / and 65 GB on the work mount. docker, podman, kind, kubectl, go, etcd and tc are installed. The repo is public.
- Writing follows unslop.

## Decisions so far
- [Destination of this session](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/6): full autonomous plan for the whole product up to the first release, no kill gate.
- [Compatibility scope of the drop-in](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/7): what kube-apiserver needs, health, basic etcdctl, TLS client certificates; open to growing into full etcd v3.
- [Consistency and durability bar](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/8): same as etcd, linearizable, acked writes and their value bytes survive loss of a minority.
- [Implementation language](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/9): Go.
- [Judge for faster than etcd](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/10): both the etcd API level and the Kubernetes level, same hardware, 3 replicas, same durability.
- [Deployment shape](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/11): 3 nodes, one executable each, TigerBeetle inside or managed by it, stock and unpatched, never touched by operators.
- [Where tests and benchmarks run](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/12): GitHub Actions.
- [TigerBeetle: requirement or means](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/13): requirement for now. The point is to find out whether it is possible.
- [Prior art](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/2): nobody built etcd on TigerBeetle. The hard parts others hit are global revisions, ordered watches and recoverable persistence.
- [etcd semantics k8s needs vs TigerBeetle primitives](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/3): k8s subset is known; TigerBeetle gives no key strings, scans or deletes; CAS via a consume-predecessor marker.
- [Where etcd's limits are](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/4): default quota 2 GiB, about 50k writes/s with many clients in old numbers; benchmark with etcd benchmark, a CAS workload, ClusterLoader2, kube-burner.
- [Test tools](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/5): storage tests via adapter, ported etcd robustness checker, Hydrophone conformance on kind, tc netem chaos.
- [Supported Kubernetes and etcd versions](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/18): Kubernetes 1.35 to 1.37, report etcd 3.7.x, RangeStream returns Unimplemented at first.
- [Security of traffic between nodes](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/21): our binary tunnels TigerBeetle's TCP traffic through mTLS (distinct loopback IP per replica).
- [First release contents](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/22): v0.1.0, amd64 and arm64 binaries, multi-arch ghcr.io image, README with 3-node and kind or kubeadm setup, reports linked.
- [License](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/23): Apache-2.0.
- [Design: durable value store](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/15): two durable copies before publishing the digest in TigerBeetle; publishing in parallel is unsafe; group commit and pipelining across writes.
- [Design: TigerBeetle storage growth](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/16): per-mutation records grow without bound (16 to 824 GiB/day/replica at 1,000 to 5,000 nodes); indefinite operation needs fewer records per write or epochs.
- [Packaging stock TigerBeetle](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/17): go:embed the stock binary and supervise it; 3 replicas tolerate any one loss; 32 MiB grid cache is about 2.1 GiB per replica.
- [Benchmark scale on GitHub runners](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/19): free runners, etcd and tigerstore one after the other, 5 repetitions, labelled (being revisited in [Benchmark venue that can show a large gain](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/31)).
- [Test layers and the release gate](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/20): own seeded Go fault proxy on every link plus netem, storage tests, ported linearizability checker, full conformance, chaos with the checker running; all gate the release.
- [Why etcd is slow](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/26): CPU-bound per-request work (gRPC plus protobuf about half the leader CPU), fsync matters little; disk stalls delay heartbeats through the shared Raft loop.
- [Mass deletes in Kubernetes](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/27): 1 DeleteCollection worker and 2 round trips per object; 16 workers made 50k deletes 3.5x faster on unchanged etcd.
- [Hardware limits](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/28): primitive costs measured on a 4-CPU ARM runner.
- [Route to a faster etcd](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/30): new store on go.etcd.io/raft with fully new custom storage, designed from single-core limits. TigerBeetle dropped.
- [Single region or wide-area clusters](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/29): single region, tested with 1 to 10 ms between nodes.
- [Benchmark venue](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/31): always free GitHub runners, one pinned core per replica and one for the load generator.
- [Plan outcomes and their order](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/34): correct core under deterministic simulation, real Kubernetes, brutal real-process chaos, wicked fast, release; then perpetual optimization until exactly 2026-10-14 00:00 Europe/Amsterdam (2026-10-13T22:00Z).
- [Done when for the speed outcome](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/35): no numeric target and no stop rule, optimize until the deadline, be bold; workers and manager ask GPT-6 Astra for second opinions throughout.
- [Red team](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/36): GPT-6 Astra red team, chaos for durability and correctness only, no security or exploit work.
- [Design changes during the plan](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/37): the manager owns large architecture decisions with Astra second opinions; workers message it only for large decisions.
- [How the optimization phase works](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/38): tournament of bold ideas; use Opus fully until its reset at the deadline; Astra is free but writes bad code; use runner wait time to build other designs; delete losing worktrees locally, keep their branches on GitHub.
- [Parallel work against the deadline](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/39): outcomes merge in order, up to 3 workers in parallel on independent pieces.
- [Deadline and releases](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/40): v0.1.0 for the first working release, a tag per merged improvement, the deadline is a pause.
- [PR review depth](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/41): two reviewers for outcomes 1 to 5, one Astra correctness reviewer in optimization.
- [Design: core store from single-core limits](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/32): starting design merged from Opus and Astra: Raft log as value store, packed self-clocked entries, one owner core per node, TLS and gRPC on every node, consistent checkpoints, arena B+tree; first experiments are a lean generator plus custom transport, core loop with real fsync, index at 10M keys, compression.
- [Design: deterministic simulation and chaos testing](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/33): starting test design merged: event and effect core, stock raft made deterministic with cryptotest.SetGlobalRandom, byte-level disk and stream network faults, crashes in recovery, erase-one-disk checks, gray nodes with numeric bounds, Porcupine plus strict watch checker, planted bugs, real-process chaos.
- [Rename manager to architect](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/42): the manager is the architect.
- [Roles of Opus and Astra](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/43): only Opus writes merged code; at most 4 Astra at once; Sol unlimited; agents failing on a cybersecurity flag are deleted and that path is not retried.
- [Improvement tags and pause](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/44): v0.1.1, v0.1.2, ... per improvement; pause at the deadline.
- [Load generator and speed metrics](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/45): own lean generator for both stores plus server CPU per op; one test per runner job, many short jobs.
- [Owner design directions](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/53): single-threaded committer without locks fed by helper threads, responses prepared before commit and released at commit, free encrypted node-to-node transport (UDP, QUIC or TCP, by measurement), explicit batching analysis.
- [Core layout on the runner](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/54): architect picks the core layout per benchmark, identical for etcd, reported; also run on this host now and then.
- [Playbook review rounds](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/46): three reviewers' findings decided by the owner in rounds 12 to 14 (comments on the playbook): merge and worker fixes, skeleton first, deadline in every prompt, architect-only Astra, manual release workflow, lint set that may be broken for performance, max objects with etcd at 8 GiB and uncapped.

## Execution
Each outcome issue is blocked by the one before. The plan runs by [Playbook: run plan 1](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/46):
1. [Correct core under deterministic simulation](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/47)
2. [Real Kubernetes on tigerstore](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/48)
3. [Brutal real-process chaos](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/49)
4. [Measured and faster](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/50)
5. [Release v0.1.0](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/51)
6. [Perpetual optimization until the pause](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/52)

## Not yet specified
Nothing. Every branch of the map is decided or written into the plan.

## Out of scope
- TigerBeetle: no key strings or scans and permanent records that grow without bound under Kubernetes churn; dropped in [Route to a faster etcd](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/30). Its earlier tickets ([#13](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/13), [#14](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/14), [#16](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/16), [#17](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/17), [#21](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/21) tunnel, [#24](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/24)) no longer apply.
- Forking etcd: capped by etcd's per-request structure ([#30](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/30)).
